capabilities.name: Diary Entry Recording
capabilities.notes: No evidence of diary entry recording functionality. XERJ is a search engine, not a diary management system.

capabilities.name: Diary Search
capabilities.notes: XERJ provides general-purpose search (BM25, vector, hybrid) which could technically be used to search diary entries if indexed. However, it lacks specific diary domain features like unit/track/location linking or structured diary entry schemas.

capabilities.name: Full-Text Search
capabilities.notes: BM25 full-text search is a core capability, evidenced by source code and documentation.

capabilities.name: Vector Search
capabilities.notes: Vector search is supported via optional neural embedders.

capabilities.name: Elasticsearch-Compatible API
capabilities.notes: API conforms to Elasticsearch-compatible protocol on port 9200.

capabilities.name: MCP Server Integration
capabilities.notes: Native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server support for agent integration.

constraints: Requires Linux (Debian trixie-slim for glibc compatibility)
Binds to loopback by default; container requires explicit 0.0.0.0 binding
Optional GPU not required but neural embedder available as opt-in

assumptions: Assumes diary entries can be indexed as standard documents in XERJ's search index
Assumes unit/track/location metadata can be stored as custom fields in the index schema
Assumes HTTPS POST submission can be handled via XERJ's existing ingestion pipeline or a wrapper service

evidence.claim: XERJ provides BM25 full-text, vector, and hybrid search capabilities
Elasticsearch-compatible API is available on port 9200
XERJ indexes code, docs, logs, JSONL/CSV and PDFs

validation.judge_notes: REVISE: [critical] The passport claims 'full' coverage for Vector Search based on 'optional neural embedders'. However, the README explicitly states the default embedder is 'lexical, offline' and neural embedders are 'opt-in, downloads ~90 MB'. Declaring full capability without the optional dependency present is misleading. The evidence_status 'declared' relies on README marketing text rather than code verification of the vector search implementation itself. | [high] The claim of ES-compatibility is marked 'declared' with evidence from README and Dockerfile. The Dockerfile only exposes port 9200; it does not contain code verifying the API protocol conformance. While the README mentions 'ES-YAML conformance', the passport's own evidence section lists this claim as 'verified: false'. A 'full' coverage claim requires stronger evidence than just a port exposure and marketing badges. | [high] The passport claims full MCP support based on README and dsh/package.json. The package.json describes a 'DeepSeek Harness (dsh) profile bundle' that 'inserts the xerj MCP server'. This suggests MCP is an integration feature or requires a specific harness, not necessarily a native, standalone capability of the core engine. The evidence_status 'declared' is weak for a 'full' coverage claim. | [medium] The claim is marked 'verified' with evidence from README and search.rs. However, the provided evidence_refs are documentation/marketing (README) and a CLI client wrapper (search.rs), not the core indexing/search engine implementation code (e.g., xerj-fts crate). Verification should ideally point to the core logic. | [medium] The passport lists license as 'apache-2.0'. The LICENSE file excerpt is truncated in the evidence ('...Legal Entity" shall mean the union of the acting entity and all'). While likely correct, the evidence provided is incomplete for a definitive audit.

description: XERJ is a Rust-based AI search engine and MCP server providing BM25 full-text, vector, and hybrid search capabilities with an Elasticsearch-compatible API. It indexes code, docs, logs, JSONL/CSV, and PDFs for agent memory and RAG.
deployment_constraints: Requires Linux (Debian trixie-slim for glibc compatibility)
Binds to loopback by default; container requires explicit 0.0.0.0 binding
Optional GPU not required but neural embedder available as opt-in
known_gaps: No native diary entry data model or schema
No support for linking entries to units, tracks, or map locations as first-class relationships
No diary-specific search filters or faceting beyond generic XERJ search capabilities
No built-in HTTPS POST endpoint specifically for diary submission (requires external wrapper)
risks: License: Apache-2.0 is permissive but requires attribution
Maturity: Release candidate (rc.102) indicates ongoing development; API stability not guaranteed
Maintenance: Active project with recent commits, but diary-specific adaptation is untested

adaptation_assumptions: Assumes diary entries can be indexed as standard documents in XERJ's search index
Assumes unit/track/location metadata can be stored as custom fields in the index schema
Assumes HTTPS POST submission can be handled via XERJ's existing ingestion pipeline or a wrapper service
